days_ago.description: Only launches within the last N days, 1–365 (default 30). Use 7 for this week, 30 for this month, 90 for this quarter, 365 for this year. Older launches are out of range; semantic_product_search with recency "all_time" finds products of any age by topic, ranked by relevance rather than launch date.

query.description: Short noun-phrase query — 3 to 8 words, no conjunctions, no conversational filler ("product that", "tool for", "I want"). Products are embedded from structured summaries covering product type, capabilities, problem solved, target audience, and use cases, so queries match best when they mirror that shape: <core-capability> <optional audience> <optional form-factor>. Only include a form factor (cli tool, terminal ui, mobile app, chrome extension, self-hosted service) when the user explicitly asks for one or clearly implies it — never invent one. Same rule for audience (developers, small teams, founders, freelancers): include only when the user names or implies it. Good: "monitor ai agents" (form factor unspecified), "self-hosted analytics small teams" (audience + form factor specified), "cli tool share ai coding sessions developers" (all three specified). Bad: "web platform monitor ai agents operations" when the user just said "a product that monitors AI agents" — the form factor was fabricated. Longer multi-clause queries collapse the neighborhood and return fewer results.

date.description: Period in YYYY-MM-DD (day), YYYY-Www (ISO week), YYYY-MM (month), or YYYY (year) format. E.g. "2024-11-14", "2024-W46", "2024-11", "2024".

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked products (default: 5, max: 8).
